Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the run chase! The umpires are back out in the middle and so are the players of West Indies. It will be the pairing of Nishan Madushka and Avishka Fernando to open the innings for Sri Lanka. Gudakesh Motie will get proceedings underway with the ball. Let's go...
... The Run Chase ...

It should be a comfortable pursuit for the hosts, but cricket is unpredictable, and the West Indies will be hoping to mount a strong defense. Let's see how the game unfolds after the break. Sri Lanka will walk out to chase 190 runs in 44 overs to seal a series ODI win over West Indies after winning the T20 series already. Will West Indies let that happen? Let's find out, in the Run Chase coming up.

At 58/8, it looked like West Indies were headed for a catastrophic collapse, but Rutherford and Motie had other ideas. Rutherford played a valiant knock of 80 runs, while Motie provided crucial support with an unbeaten 52. Their 119-run stand gave West Indies a fighting chance, posting a total that looked improbable earlier in the innings. Sri Lanka's bowlers did most of the hard work early on, but their fielding woes returned to haunt them. Dropped catches, particularly three missed opportunities to dismiss Rutherford, allowed the visitors to extend their innings. Despite these lapses, Sri Lanka still have a relatively modest target of 190 to chase.

The first innings of the 2nd ODI at Pallekele comes to a close with West Indies being bowled out for 189. After being reduced to a dismal 58/8, the Shai Hope-led side managed a remarkable recovery, thanks to a brilliant partnership between Sherfane Rutherford and Gudakesh Motie. West Indies were off to a shaky start after being put in to bat by Sri Lankan captain Charith Asalanka on a pitch similar to the previous ODI. Rain delayed the start by two hours, and once play began, the West Indies batting line-up crumbled, with wickets falling regularly.

Commentary.Commentary: Drinks break! Just over an hour played here in Pallekele and the players are given a breather. Sri Lanka have made excellent use of the conditions with the spinners wreaking havoc and Asitha Fernando also made sure that the early seaming conditions didn't go to waste, picking up a couple of wickets. West Indies have yet again found themselves relying big time on the middle order and this pair of Sherfane Rutherford and Roston Chase is exactly what you want in a crisis but it is a big ask for them to take the Windies to some sort of a defendable total from here.

Commentary.Commentary: Starts off with a flighted ball, a bit full and around off, Shai Hope strokes it wide of extra cover and sets off for the quick single. Wanindu Hasaranga there moves across quickly and throws the ball on the slide to the bowler's end and misses. They get the single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.1: Dunith Wellalage to Shai Hope, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Full and around off, some movement in the air as well, Shai Hope looks to cover drive but gets it off the inner half of the blade onto the leg side for a quick single. Just a run and a wicket off that over.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.6: Asitha Fernando to Shai Hope, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Ooh, just going down leg! Nagging length on middle, slanting back in a fair bit, Shai Hope looks to flick but is beaten for pace and gets pinged on the back leg.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.5: Asitha Fernando to Shai Hope, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Shai Hope, the skipper of West Indies is the next batter in.

OUT! CAUGHT AND BOWLED! Asitha Fernando gets rid of the other Windies opener now and Sri Lanka have their second wicket. Fernando bowls a heavy short ball, banging it in halfway down the pitch around off and at 135 clicks. Brandon King looks to take on the pull but gets rushed and the ball ends up coming off the splice of the bat. It lobs up just to the left of the bowler who takes a simple catch and West Indies are 17/2 inside the first 4 overs.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.4: Asitha Fernando to Brandon King, OUT! c & b Asitha Fernando.

Commentary.Commentary: That in-between length now, nipping back into off and middle, King hangs back and jams it out with hard hands towards mid-wicket.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.3: Asitha Fernando to Brandon King, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Pitches the ball up now on off, just getting some shape away from the right-hander, King leans on and plays it with a straight bat towards mid off.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.2: Asitha Fernando to Brandon King, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Hits the deck hard around off, angling the ball back in towards the stumps, Brandon King gets across and blocks it solidly down to mid on.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.1: Asitha Fernando to Brandon King, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Shortens the length a bit and bowls it quick on middle, Keacy Carty goes on the back foot and jams it down to mid on.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.6: Maheesh Theekshana to Keacy Carty, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Keacy Carty is the new batter at number 3 for West Indies.

OUT! BOWLED'EM! A ripper of a delivery from Maheesh Theekshana and Alick Athanaze has to walk back early. Theekshana comes around the stumps to the left-hander and bowls a lovely off-break delivery. This is tossed up on middle and leg, curving in, dipping as well and then it just grips and rips away after pitching. Athanaze leans to defend down the line but the ball beats the outside edge and knocks over the top of off. Sri Lanka get an early breakthrough here.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.5: Maheesh Theekshana to Alick Athanaze, OUT! b Maheesh Theekshana.

Commentary.Commentary: Flatter delivery on off, this one turns back in a bit, King gets pegged back and just dabs it down to fine leg for a run.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.4: Maheesh Theekshana to Brandon King, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Begging to be hit! Floated up, full and wide, the attempted off-break again, Brandon King reaches out and creams it through the big gap at covers for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.3: Maheesh Theekshana to Brandon King, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: The carrom ball now, on off and middle, staying a bit low, King is taken aback but manages to keep it out.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.2: Maheesh Theekshana to Brandon King, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Darted in at 97 clicks, fuller and right at the stumps, King gets a good stride in to defend.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.1: Maheesh Theekshana to Brandon King, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Hits the deck hard, bowling it around off, Athanaze just stands tall and pushes it away to covers.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.6: Asitha Fernando to Alick Athanaze, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Full and outside off, not quite full enough though. King looks to lean on and drive but gets it off the inside edge towards deep square leg and picks up a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.5: Asitha Fernando to Brandon King, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Bowled back of a length and around off, King looks to hammer it on the off side but mistimes it back onto the deck.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.4: Asitha Fernando to Brandon King, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Lovely timing on that one but Janith Liyanage should have done better. Pitched up on off, looking to swing it away, King gets nicely forward and pushes it off the middle of the bat and wide od mid off. Liyanage dives over it and the ball rolls away to the fence.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.3: Asitha Fernando to Brandon King, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: On a good length and around the fifth stump line, King gets his front foot across and plays it on the up and straight to cover-point.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.2: Asitha Fernando to Brandon King, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Off the mark right away! Pitched-up delivery, trying to angle it across the left-hander, Alick Athanaze gets on the front foot and drives it off the outer half of the blade to wide of deep third and picks up a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.1: Asitha Fernando to Alick Athanaze, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Asitha Fernando to share the new ball with Maheesh Theekshana for Sri Lanka.

FOUR! Too wide, it was the attempted off-spinner which didn't turn, Brandon King waited on the back foot and slapped it away well behind point for the first boundary of the chase. West Indies 6/0 at the end of the first over.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.6: Maheesh Theekshana to Brandon King, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: On a length on middle and off, straightening down the pitch, King watches it well and blocks it off.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.5: Maheesh Theekshana to Brandon King, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Pushed through flatter and wide of the off stump, King lets the ball come on and punches it sweetly towards cover.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.4: Maheesh Theekshana to Brandon King, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Halt! Kusal Mendis gets a hit on his right thumb from a throw by Avishka Fernando. Gets the required medical attention and is ready to wear the gloves back.
There's that regulation carrom ball, a bit fuller and straighter on the stumps, King works it around the corner for a couple of runs and West Indies are up and running here.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.3: Maheesh Theekshana to Brandon King, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Big turn there! Just a tad full and outside off, King looks to play it off the back foot but it turns back in a long way and catches him on the pads.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.2: Maheesh Theekshana to Brandon King, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Hint of turn straightaway! Starts with a quicker one, bowled short and outside off, this one comes back in. Brandon King rocks back and taps it away toward cover.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.1: Maheesh Theekshana to Brandon King, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Right then! After the delay, the match starts as the players and the umpires make their way to the middle! Alick Athanaze and Brandon King are the opening batters from West Indies on the pitch to start the innings for their side. Maheesh Theekshana has the new ball in hand for Sri Lanka. Spin into the attack from the start! Let's play!

PITCH REPORT - Tino Mawayo is pitchside. Says that it is the same one from the previous game and it is abrasive with minimal grass cover. Adds that it is a good batting surface and there might be some swing but there will be turn for sure.

Shai Hope, the West Indies skipper, expresses that they would have opted to bowl first as well, given the weather conditions. He acknowledges that the conditions in the previous match were challenging for batting but emphasizes the need to perform better today. Hope mentions that while certain things are beyond their control, the focus is on improving in all three departments. He confirms that West Indies will field the same XI for the game.

Charith Asalanka, the captain of Sri Lanka says that they will bowl first given the weather conditions. He adds that he would like a better bowling side in order to pick up more wickets. Informs that there is one change with Maheesh Theekshana coming in for Jeffrey Vandersay.

Sri Lanka (Playing XI) - Avishka Fernando, Nishan Madushka, Kusal Mendis (WK), Kamindu Mendis, Charith Asalanka (C), Sadeera Samarawickrama, Janith Liyanage, Wanindu Hasaranga, Dunith Wellalage, Asitha Fernando, Maheesh Theekshana (In for Jeffrey Vandersay).

West Indies (Playing XI) - Brandon King, Alick Athanaze, Shai Hope (C) (WK), Keacy Carty, Sherfane Rutherford, Romario Shepherd, Roston Chase, Alzarri Joseph, Gudakesh Motie, Jayden Seales, Hayden Walsh.
TOSS - The Sri Lankan skipper, Charith Asalanka wins the coin toss and elects to have a BOWL first!
UPDATE - 10.43 am GMT - Moments away from the TOSS! It's now a 44-over game, and both the skippers are on the pitchside for the coin toss.

UPDATE - 10.40 am GMT - It seems that the drizzle has stopped and the covers are coming off. Also, we have a prompt toss time which is going to be 10.45 am GMT. Play will now begin at 11 am GMT which means we have only lost a further 15 minutes from the revised time. We might not even lose more overs for now if the game does start at 11 am.

UPDATE - 10.19 am GMT - Uh, oh! Right on cue, just when the toss was about to take place, the drizzle is back. This means that the toss is delayed yet again and for now, only the pitch is under covers which, hopefully, means that it shouldn't be a full-fledged delay and rather a short one but who knows. Stay tuned as we bring you further updates on the toss and ground conditions.

UPDATE - 10.06 am GMT - Excellent news coming in from Pallekele as the toss is scheduled for 10.15 am GMT, just a few minutes from now. The match is then scheduled to start at 10.45 am GMT and it will be a 45-overs-a-side contest. Strap yourselves in as we gear up for the toss and team updates.

UPDATE - 9.45 am GMT - Some good news coming from the ground as a few of the covers are being removed. We can only hope that the rain stays away now so that the clean up job can be done and we can get the ball rolling with the toss and a start time soon. Stick around for more updates.

UPDATE - 9.23 am GMT - A few sources show that the rain has stopped in Pallekele for a few minutes now but the covers aren't going anywhere. Maybe the ground staff expect some more inclement weather or they are just making sure that the water is first completely removed from the covers and none of it seeps into the ground. Whatever it is, let's hope that it is positive.

Meanwhile, a bit up and to the east in Bangladesh, the 1st Test match between Bangladesh and South Africa is going on. Rain affected that game as well today on Day 3, halting the hosts' second-innings comeback. However, action is about to get back underway right about now, so, you can switch tabs and catch our coverage of that game. But don't be gone for too long though as there's plenty of action to look forward to in Pallekele.

UPDATE - 8.53 am GMT - The broadcasters come live and we can see that there is just a slight drizzle at the moment but the entire ground is covered as there was heavy rain earlier in the day. The ground staff is working to get the water off the covers diligently and the weather is just starting to look a bit clear. However, it does look like this starting delay will be a prolonged one. Let's hope that the weather keeps improving and we can get a starting time soon. Stick around for more updates.

UPDATE - 8.35 am GMT - Toss was scheduled for 8.30 am GMT which was five minutes back but sources have confirmed that the toss has officially been delayed due to rain. Hopefully, it is not a long delay, so, stay tuned as we bring you the latest updates from the ground.

Heading into the second ODI, West Indies will be looking to regroup, especially their top order, which needs to step up if they want to level the series. While their performance was clinical in the opener, Sri Lanka had moments of vulnerability and will aim to address those issues to maintain their dominance. With rain still in question, the second ODI might be interrupted but we hope for a fair result at the end of the day. Will Sri Lanka continue their winning streak and close out the series, or can West Indies fight back and force a thrilling decider? We’ll soon find out! Stay tuned!

In the first ODI, Sri Lanka’s resilience shone through, despite being challenged at moments. The West Indies’ top order faltered early, but a gritty middle-order fightback, led by Sherfane Rutherford and supported by Keacy Carty and Roston Chase, kept their hopes alive. However, rain intervened, halting their momentum and leaving them with a DLS adjusted total to defend. Despite the wet ball conditions making it tough for their bowlers, the West Indies managed to pick up three early wickets, applying pressure on Sri Lanka. But the hosts stayed composed, with a key fourth-wicket partnership between Nishan Madushka and Charith Asalanka helping them ease to victory.

A warm welcome to every one of you joining us here today. Sri Lanka will look to secure a white-ball series double over West Indies as the two teams face off in the second ODI of their three-match series at the Pallekele International Cricket Stadium in Kandy. After a successful comeback to win the T20I series and claiming victory in a rain-hit first ODI, the hosts are in prime position to wrap up the series. Meanwhile, the West Indies, eager to stay alive, will be looking to bounce back and force a decider in the final match of the series.
... MATCH DAY ...

After a commanding victory in the first ODI, Sri Lanka will take on West Indies in the second ODI at the Pallekele International Cricket Stadium in Kandy. While Sri Lanka will aim to maintain their momentum and seal the series, the visitors will be eager to bounce back, level the series, and force a decider. In the opener, the West Indies’ top order faltered, but a spirited middle-order recovery led by Sherfane Rutherford and supported by Keacy Carty and Roston Chase gave them hope. Unfortunately, rain disrupted their momentum, leaving them with a DLS-adjusted score to defend. The wet ball conditions added to their challenges, but they still picked up three early wickets to build some pressure. However, a gritty fourth-wicket partnership between Nishan Madushka and Charith Asalanka took the game away, helping Sri Lanka cruise to victory. While batting conditions improved after the rain, the West Indies will need to factor that in and come harder in this match to keep the series alive. On the other hand, Sri Lanka, though clinical, had moments where they were tested and will want to iron out any flaws to get closer to their peak performance. Can the West Indies regroup and take the series to a decider, or will Sri Lanka wrap it up with another win at home? We’ll find out soon!
